svg.title: Deeper Roots: from Omar Khayyam and Desiderius Erasmus to Saleem A. Al Dajani
svg.desc: Two older streams of an academic lineage recorded by the Mathematics Genealogy Project. One runs from Omar Khayyam through Sharaf al-Dīn al-Marwazī, Kamāl al-Dīn Ibn Yūnus, Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī, Shams al-Dīn al-Bukhārī, Gregory Chioniadis, Manuel Bryennios, Theodore Metochites, Gregory Palamas, Nilos Kabasilas, Demetrios Kydones, Georgios Gemistos Plethon, Basilios Bessarion, Johannes Argyropoulos, Jacques Lefèvre d’Étaples, Melchior Wolmar, Theodore Beza, Antonius Thysius. The other runs from Desiderius Erasmus through Jakob Milich, Erasmus Reinhold, Valentine Naibod, Rudolph Snellius, Jacobus Arminius, Gilbert Jacchaeus, Franck P. Burgersdijk. They meet at Arnold Senguerdius and continue through Wolferd Senguerdius, Herman Boerhaave, Henry Bracken, John Dawson, Adam Sedgwick, then six more generations to David E. Keyes and on to Saleem A. Al Dajani.
svg.text: Two older streams, from Omar Khayyam and Desiderius Erasmus, flowing to today
Anderson · Krook · Eddington · Whitehead · Routh · Hopkins
Erasmus in 21 steps and Khayyam in 31, by the shortest routes recorded in the Mathematics Genealogy Project. Places and years drawn from those records.
Early links reflect recorded mentorship and scholarly transmission, not modern doctoral advising.
